transcript: This is part of a new series called Serious Advice in a Silly Sweatshirt. I don't know if it's going to last, but we're running with it. One of the things that we always told our daughters is no 16-year-old girl is any man's solution to a problem. What do I mean by that? I mean if you're at a gas station and a grown man comes up to you and goes, Hey, I have a flat tire or I need some gas money or around the corner there's a problem. You're not their solution. No 16-year-old girl solves a 40-year-old man's problem. They are weaponizing your empathy against you. They are trying to trick you with your kindness. So we said to them always, if somebody's on the side of the road and you're a 16-year-old girl, drive on by. If somebody comes up to you at a gas station or downtown and says, hey, I really need your help, nobody who's in their 30s, 40s, or 50s goes, who would help me fix this situation? I know a 14-year-old girl. I'll get her to help. Move along. Now, some people said, oh, that's fear-based. No, no, no. That's wisdom-based. You can have wisdom and courage at the same time.
